title: Pleading Face Emoji 🥺 Meaning: The Puppy-Dog Eyes
description: What does 🥺 mean? The pleading face emoji begs, melts at cute things and plays shy with 👉👈. Here is how to read it from friends, a crush or a stranger.
summary: The 🥺 pleading face has huge, glossy eyes and a small frown, the classic puppy-dog look. People use it to beg for a favor, to show they are touched by something sweet, or to act cute and needy on purpose. It is rarely about real sadness; it is about wanting affection or a yes.
meaning: The original purpose is right in the name: pleading. “Can you pick me up 🥺” puts on an exaggerated sad face to make a request harder to refuse. Everyone involved knows it is a performance, and that is the charm. It lets the sender ask for something while joking about how badly they want it.

Just as often, nobody is asking for anything. 🥺 is the reflex response to a puppy video, a thoughtful gift or a friend saying something unexpectedly kind. In that role it means “my heart,” a feeling of being moved to the point of going soft. Since 2021 the 🥹 face holding back tears has taken over some of this territory, but 🥺 remains the more common choice.

Added in 2018, it became a defining emoji of the following few years, largely through the “🥺👉👈” combination, in which two index fingers touch like a shy anime character working up the nerve to speak. That pose spread across TikTok and Twitter and turned the emoji into shorthand for timid, needy or submissive energy, including in flirtatious and sexual contexts.

Its popularity produced a backlash. Some people find it cloying or manipulative, and it is frequently used with heavy irony: mock sympathy for a complaint that does not deserve any, or a sarcastic “is someone upset 🥺” in an argument. Reading it correctly depends on who is sending it and whether the situation calls for tenderness at all.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: Between friends and partners it softens requests and apologies. “Sorry I forgot to call 🥺” asks to be forgiven without a heavy conversation. It also marks affection, as in “I miss you 🥺.” The more of them in a row, the less serious the plea and the more the sender is simply being playful.

contexts.label: From a crush
contexts.body: Someone who sends you 🥺 is letting their guard down. It can mean they want your attention, they found what you said sweet, or they are hinting that they would like to see you. Because the emoji is deliberately vulnerable, people seldom send it to someone they feel neutral about, though a few use it with everybody.

contexts.label: On TikTok and Instagram
contexts.body: Comments like “the way he looked at her 🥺” show the viewer was moved. Fans also post it under photos of celebrities as a kind of adoring whimper. In ironic corners of the internet it mocks oversensitivity, so a 🥺 reply to an angry post is usually taunting, not comforting.

contexts.label: At work
contexts.body: It can come across as childish or as emotional pressure. A “could you cover my shift 🥺” to a close coworker is fine; the same message to a manager or client undercuts you. A plain “please” does the job better in anything professional.

examples.text: Can you bring me fries on your way home 🥺
examples.meaning: A playful, exaggerated plea for a small favor.

examples.text: You remembered my interview was today 🥺
examples.meaning: The sender is touched that someone paid attention.
Shyly working up to asking someone out.
Overwhelmed by how cute an animal is.

examples.text: Aw did the game not go your way 🥺
examples.meaning: Sarcastic mock sympathy aimed at someone who is complaining.
Asking for forgiveness while trying to look too sweet to stay angry at.

combos.meaning: The shy fidget: nervously asking for something or confessing a crush.
Deeply touched; a soft, heartfelt thank-you or declaration of affection.
Begging outright, usually for a favor or for plans not to be canceled.
So moved or so overwhelmed by cuteness that the sender is beside themselves.

confusedWith.difference: 🥹 smiles while its eyes fill, so it reads as pride, gratitude or happy tears. 🥺 frowns slightly and looks up, which adds a note of asking or neediness that 🥹 lacks.
😢 has an actual tear and expresses real, if mild, sadness. 🥺 has no tear at all; its wet-looking eyes are about appealing to someone, not about being hurt.
😳 is a startled blush in reaction to something. 🥺 is an appeal directed at someone. Both pair with 👉👈, but 😳 feels embarrassed and 🥺 feels like begging.

avoid: Leave it out of professional requests, where it can look like guilt-tripping.
Do not use it to respond to someone's serious grief or bad news; it can seem cutesy or self-centered.
Be careful sending it to people you do not know well, since many read it as flirtatious.
design: A yellow face with very large, shiny eyes angled upward, furrowed brows and a small downturned mouth. Designs are closely aligned across platforms: all of them rely on oversized eyes with bright highlights to suggest tears that are about to form. The eyes are larger than on almost any other face emoji, which is what makes it instantly recognizable even at small sizes.

faqs.q: What does 🥺 mean from a girl?
faqs.a: Most often she is being affectionate, asking for something sweetly, or saying that something you did touched her. With 👉👈 it suggests shyness. On its own it is warm, but it is not proof of romantic interest; plenty of people send it to close friends.

faqs.q: What does 🥺 mean from a guy?
faqs.a: Usually that he is comfortable being soft around you: missing you, wanting your attention or reacting to something kind. Guys who use it tend to reserve it for people they like, though ironic use among friends is common too.

It imitates someone looking up with big eyes while tapping their index fingers together, a gesture of shyness borrowed from anime. It means the sender is nervous about asking for something or admitting a feeling.

It can be. The emoji signals vulnerability and a wish for attention, which is why it shows up in flirting and in more explicitly sexual, submissive joking online. In everyday texts, though, it more often just means “please” or “that's so sweet.”
Not really. It borrows the look of someone about to cry, but people use it for begging, tenderness and cuteness. For actual sadness, 😢, 😞 or 😭 are clearer.
